title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Verdant Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE team ran a POC scoping call with Verdant Health to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and deployment decision criteria (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key concerns: PHI handling, latency SLOs for clinical summarization, cost per 1k tokens, timeline for an 8-week POC, and security documentation (SOC2, VPC/KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share security checklist and pricing estimate, run a small CPU/GPU benchmark with representative prompts, and schedule a bench+demo in 10 days.
topics: Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Sofia Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Gupta (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Verdant Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Dr. Priya Nair (Security), Ethan Moore (PM)

[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Sofia our solutions engineer and Ravi from customer success. How are you all?
[00:10] Maya Patel: Hi, hi, thanks Alex. Doing well. Appreciate you guys fitting us in.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: Yep, thanks. We got a few folks on our side, we'll keep it tight.
[00:22] Alex Mercer: Great. Objective for today is to scope a POC — align on success criteria, get an approximate workload size, agree benchmark profiles and timelines, and discuss which deployment mode makes sense for Verdant, hosted versus dedicated reserved capacity versus private (VPC / on-prem).
[00:38] Sofia Chen: I'll jump in on the technical assumptions, e.g., what your prompt latencies look like today and how many concurrent sessions we should plan for.
[00:46] Ethan Moore: Quick context: we're a digital health app for post-op follow ups. The core workload is clinical note summarization and triage flags. We expect peak concurrency around office hours, maybe 150 concurrent requests, average prompt length 500 tokens, and responses around 300 tokens. Latency target is sub-1.5s for the triage API and under 3s for summary.
[01:10] Sofia Chen: OK that's helpful. When you say 150 concurrent requests, is that sustained or bursts?
[01:15] Ethan Moore: More like 10-15 minute bursts during morning intake, so bursty but predictable.
[01:21] Maya Patel: Also super important — all of this touches PHI. We need encryption at rest, audit logs, and KMS integration. Ideally we'd keep data in our AWS account or on-prem.
[01:32] Dr. Priya Nair: And we need to understand retention policies, and if Redwood can attest to SOC2 and provide audit logs for each request.
[01:40] Alex Mercer: Totally — Redwood supports SOC2 Type II, we provide detailed audit logs and KMS integration for dedicated and private deployments. Hosted mode can be configured with customer-managed KMS for some plans; we'll share the security checklist.
[01:54] Ravi Gupta: I'll follow up with the SOC2 report and our network diagram after the call.
[01:59] Liam O'Connor: Great. From an infra POV, we need to understand the CPU/GPU expectations. Our initial thought was to try hosted to get started, but if PHI requires private control plane then we might need a private or dedicated setup.
[02:14] Sofia Chen: Right — quick high level tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to onboard and lowest friction for an 8-week POC; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation (dedicated GPUs, reserved capacity), and private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the most control for PHI but requires longer lead time and infra coordination. We'll map that to your success criteria and compliance needs.
[02:35] Maya Patel: What's the typical lead time for dedicated vs private?
[02:39] Alex Mercer: Dedicated can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private (VPC peering or on-prem appliance) is usually 4-8 weeks for VPC and longer for on-prem, due to networking and security approvals.
[02:52] Ethan Moore: For POC success criteria we'd want: 1) accuracy of clinical summarization within our eval set (ROUGE / clinician review), 2) latency below the SLOs, 3) cost per 1k tokens within projected budget, and 4) auditability and encryption. Is that reasonable?
[03:12] Sofia Chen: Yes. For accuracy we'll run a quality eval with your gold prompts + sample responses; for latency we'll run three benchmark profiles (low-latency triage, medium summary, high-length batch). And cost we can estimate from tokens and model choice, and show tradeoffs like quantized models on dedicated to reduce cost.
[03:30] Maya Patel: About the model — are you proposing an open model or Redwood managed ones? We care about determinism and reproducibility for clinical audits.
[03:40] Alex Mercer: We can host curated open models from our catalog, or you can bring your own model. For production and auditability we recommend pinning a model version and using Redwood's rollout control so you can reproduce outputs. We'll document the exact model+weights used during the POC.
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: One nit — do you support KV cache or prefix caching? Our summaries re-use context a lot.
[04:02] Sofia Chen: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching across sessions. For dedicated and private deployments you get more control over cache sizing and persistence, which helps reduce token costs. In hosted you get automatic workload-aware caching but it's multi-tenant and policies vary by tier.
[04:18] Maya Patel: On compliance: do you have customers that handle PHI currently? Any health customers we can reference?
[04:24] Alex Mercer: We have several health customers on dedicated and private deployments; I can share sanitized case notes and a reference list — subject to NDA. We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:34] Ethan Moore: For benchmarks, what do you recommend we run?
[04:37] Sofia Chen: We'll propose three benchmark profiles: (1) Triage (short prompts, 1-2 s target), (2) Summarization (500 tokens in, 300 tokens out), (3) Bulk batch processing (overnight, high throughput). We'll run each across hosted and a dedicated config so you can compare latency and cost.
[04:56] Maya Patel: How do you measure RPS to GPU utilization? We need to size the dedicated pool appropriately so we don't overcommit.
[05:03] Sofia Chen: We'll ask you for sample traffic (RPS distribution over 24h) and typical input/response lengths. Sofia: then we run microbenchmarks to map tokens/sec to GPUs based on model size and quantization. We also provide recommended autoscaling policies — e.g., baseline capacity for steady 100 RPS and burst capacity for 150-200.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: For the POC we can provide 48 hours of logs and a synthetic 1-week load profile to test bursts.
[05:29] Alex Mercer: Perfect. That will let us recommend either a hosted pilot with higher tier or a small dedicated footprint.
[05:36] Dr. Priya Nair: A few security specifics: we need request-level audit logs retained for 1 year, full encryption at rest with customer KMS, SSO via SAML, RBAC and per-route access controls, and an option to keep data in their VPC or on-prem. Which of these are available in which mode?
[05:55] Alex Mercer: Short answers: audit logs — available in all modes, retention configurable (premium add-on for longer retention). Customer-managed KMS — available for dedicated and private; hosted can integrate with CMK for certain enterprise tiers. SAML SSO and RBAC — available across all control planes. VPC/on-prem — private only. We'll include a mapping doc in the security checklist.
[06:17] Ethan Moore: About cost: if we start hosted, can we estimate cost to process 100k summaries per month?
[06:23] Sofia Chen: Rough calc: if summary average output is 300 tokens and input 500 tokens that's 800 tokens per request. At 100k requests that's 80M tokens. Depending on model (e.g., 13B vs 70B) the per-token pricing ranges a lot. We'll provide a conservative estimate and an optimized estimate using quantization/dedicated pricing.
[06:44] Maya Patel: Would dedicated reduce cost per token materially?
[06:48] Alex Mercer: Yes — dedicated reserved capacity gives a lower unit cost and predictable spend, plus you can use quantized execution to further reduce GPU memory and cost. But there's a commitment and provisioning lead time. For long term with steady volume, dedicated is usually cheaper.
[07:02] Liam O'Connor: If we need PHI to remain in our VPC, then private is the only option, right?
[07:07] Alex Mercer: Correct if you require data never leaves your VPC or on-prem environment. We also offer a hybrid — private control plane with Redwood-managed model hosting in your VPC. We'll detail options.
[07:19] Maya Patel: For the POC success criteria on quality, can we do a blinded clinician review? We'll score outputs for accuracy and hallucination rate.
[07:26] Sofia Chen: Absolutely. We'll ingest your gold set, run the model outputs, and create a report showing ROUGE, BLEU if helpful, and clinician blinded review summaries. We'll include regression thresholds.
[07:37] Ethan Moore: Timeline — we're hoping to have a POC decision in 8 weeks to align with Q4 roadmap. What's realistic?
[07:44] Alex Mercer: 8 weeks is realistic for a hosted-to-dedicated path: week 0-1 define success criteria and collect prompts; week 1-2 security review and network collection; week 2-4 bench + quality evals; week 4-6 pilot on hosted or small dedicated; week 6-8 decision and possible ramp. If private or on-prem is chosen, add 2-4 weeks for network & infra.
[08:05] Maya Patel: That aligns. Can you outline the deliverables for each phase?
[08:10] Alex Mercer: Deliverables: (1) requirements doc & success criteria, (2) security pack and network checklist, (3) benchmark results (latency, cost), (4) quality eval report, (5) pilot runbook and ops playbook, (6) final recommendation and pricing.
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: On the bench we want raw p95 latency, p99, and cost per 1k tokens. Also GPU memory utilization and CPU load.
[08:34] Sofia Chen: We'll capture those metrics and provide both real-time traces and summarized dashboards.
[08:40] Maya Patel: What about model versioning and rollbacks — important for clinical auditing.
[08:44] Alex Mercer: Redwood supports model pinning, rollout controls (canary, A/B), and you can snapshot a model+weights. We also log which version served each inference for audit.
[08:56] Ethan Moore: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[08:59] Sofia Chen: Network/NAT and firewall rules can slow a private deployment. Also expectation mismatch on latency when comparing multi-tenant hosted to dedicated GPUs — we'll surface those in the benchmark. For PHI there's additional legal review which can add time.
[09:12] Dr. Priya Nair: We'll need the exact data flow diagram to show to our privacy officer.
[09:16] Alex Mercer: We'll attach a network/data-flow diagram to the security pack.
[09:19] Maya Patel: Could we do a hybrid POC: start in hosted for quick results and then run parallel bench on a small dedicated node to compare?
[09:27] Alex Mercer: Yes, that's a common pattern: quick hosted pilot to validate quality and then a dedicated bench for economics and isolation testing. That gives you production readiness data without blocking on infra.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. On metrics, besides latency and cost we want to track inference failure modes and fallback behavior. If model times out, what happens?
[09:44] Sofia Chen: We surface errors in the logs and have automatic retry/fallback policies. Can configure route-level fallbacks to a smaller model or cached answers. We'll show examples in the playbook.
[09:56] Ethan Moore: For the POC, what sample prompts will we use for the triage microbench?
[10:00] Maya Patel: We'll provide 50 canonical triage prompts and 200 summary prompts drawn from de-identified data.
[10:06] Sofia Chen: Great — please use the upload link we'll share.
[10:09] Alex Mercer: Recap and next actions: I'll send the security checklist + SOC2 + network diagram by Thursday (7/22). Sofia will run benchmarks across hosted and a small dedicated config and aim to share initial numbers by next Thursday (7/29). Maya will provide the canonical prompts and traffic profile by Friday (7/23). We'll tentatively meet 7/30 for bench review and demo. Does that work?
[10:31] Maya Patel: Yes, works for us.
[10:33] Dr. Priya Nair: I'll review the security pack and follow up with any questions.
[10:36] Liam O'Connor: One more question — do you provide SSO and role mapping that maps to our IdP attributes?
[10:42] Alex Mercer: Yes, we support SAML/SCIM provisioning and can map IdP attributes to RBAC roles. We'll include that in the ops runbook.
[10:49] Ethan Moore: Is there a sandbox API key for us to test quickly?
[10:52] Ravi Gupta: We'll create a short-lived sandbox project for you once we get the prompt set; that way you can run exploratory tests right away.
[10:59] Maya Patel: Awesome. Thanks everyone.
[11:02] Alex Mercer: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the pack and the bench schedule. Talk soon.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts: 'prefix cache' sometimes transcribed as 'pre-fix cache', 'KMS' occasionally 'K-M-S', 'SOC2' as 'sock two' in a couple spots. Occasional speaker mis-attribution (some lines marked as 'Speaker 2' in original auto-transcript).
